where: APFS: writing into a clone just made
what: On APFS the first `pwrite` into a file cloned a moment ago takes 3.5 ms whatever its size (4 KiB or 2.6 MB), and renaming that file over another takes 3.6 ms; a clone made 300 ms earlier takes 0.3 to 1 ms for the write and 0.3 ms for the rename, and a new sparse file 0.3 and 0.3 (python, 15 to 30 turns each, quiet disk). `F_FULLFSYNC` of any other file meanwhile makes them 10 and 7.5 ms. So an edit's place by clone, write, rename has a floor near 7 ms a file on a quiet disk.
cost: about 6 ms of every edit's answer on macOS (`the job's answer waits for what it still does: its outputs, being placed` 8.1 ms after this lane)
cause: my guess, unverified: the clone's transaction is still open when the write comes; the check is the same timing with the clone made earlier, which is fast
state: open: make the next edit's clone as the last place ends (off the answer's path), so an edit's place is its writes and one rename; needs the store to hold a staged clone per path, checked against the path's file as it is used
